instruction_given_to_self: Read the round-4 disagreement slice (dense vs the round-3 VA_nl; rows read in rounds 1-3 excluded). Propose 15 quality-relevant criteria. NO composite quota this round: the round-3 result killed the shape hypothesis (round 3 was 14/15 composite and returned +.0001 against round 2's 10/15 and +.0095), so criteria are authored on merit and the composite count is COUNTED AND REPORTED rather than targeted. Label-blind: `judgement` was never loaded; no criterion references acceptance or any outcome.
scale: 0-10 integer, NA if the abstract gives no evidence bearing on the criterion
shape_note: 9/15 composite, counted from the per-criterion `composite` flags below and asserted in code before scoring (round-3 lesson). Round 1 was free-form, round 2 was 10/15, round 3 was 14/15.

criteria.name: Methodological critique — a flawed practice in the field is named AND its consequence shown
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract identifies a specific defective practice in how the field evaluates, reports, or measures things, and separately whether it demonstrates what that defect costs (a wrong conclusion it produces, a method it falsely flatters); score 0-10 for BOTH together. Score low when a practice is criticised without demonstrated consequence.
criteria.rationale: R4-DH23 (recalibration methods 'can appear seemingly state-of-the-art unless calibration and prediction metrics are accompanied by additional generalization metrics'), R4-DH01 ('deterministic evaluations falsely indicate successful unlearning and alignment'), R4-DH09 ('current state-of-the-art hierarchy-aware deep classifiers do not always show practical improvement over the standard cross-entropy baseline'), R4-DH15 (the faithfulness assumption 'is often not satisfied in real-world or synthetic datasets'). Round-1 A08 scored diagnosing a failure of prior METHODS; this scores diagnosing a failure of the field's own measurement practice, which is the pattern concentrated on this slice's dense-high side.

criteria.name: Simplicity restoration — a simple or classical method is shown to match or beat elaborate recent ones
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge how simple the method being advocated is (few parts, classical, little tuning, small code change), and separately how elaborate the approaches it is shown to match or beat are; score 0-10 for the CONTRAST. Score low when a simple method beats only other simple methods, and low when the advocated method is itself elaborate.
criteria.rationale: R4-DH09 ('the classical Conditional Risk Minimization framework ... needs no extra hyperparameters and requires adding just a few lines of code to the standard cross-entropy baseline. It significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art'), R4-DH23 (trivial recalibration exposing the literature), R4-DH03 ('Is there a middle way that balances high performance with low resources? We find the answer to be yes'). Round-2 A17 scored simplicity relative to PROBLEM difficulty; this scores simplicity relative to the COMPETITION's complexity, which is a different and sharper contrast.

criteria.name: Unification — one mechanism handles problems previously treated separately
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge how many genuinely distinct problems the abstract claims to address, and separately how single the mechanism addressing them is; score 0-10 for BOTH together — high when one clean mechanism covers several previously separate problems, low for a multi-part system covering several problems and low for one mechanism covering one problem.
criteria.rationale: R4-DH27 (TERM: one tilt hyperparameter spanning outlier robustness, fairness, variance reduction and class imbalance, 'not only competitive with existing solutions tailored to these individual problems'), R4-DH13 (ULTRA: one pre-trained model inductively generalising to any KG vocabulary, tested on 57 graphs), R4-DH11 (abduction and induction united). Distinct from round-2 A16 (subsumption of prior WORK as special cases): this is subsumption of distinct PROBLEMS by one mechanism.

criteria.name: Necessity established — an ablation shows the components are actually required
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract claims particular components are essential, and separately whether it reports an ablation or controlled comparison establishing that necessity; score 0-10 for BOTH together. Score low for components asserted as key with no ablation, and low for an ablation mentioned with no necessity claim attached.
criteria.rationale: R4-DH10 ('Our ablation experiments show that both the dynamic architecture and NeRF distillation are critical to the expressivity of HyperFields'), R4-DH12 ('we show that simpler alternatives for representing the inverse Hessians worsen performance'), R4-DH16 ('naive strategies ... give limited improvement and can even lead to negative transfer'). Deliberately paired with a shallow Track-B probe that merely counts the word 'ablation', so the audit can be tested on whether it separates the claim-plus-evidence structure from the keyword.

criteria.name: The motivating observation is itself reported as a finding
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract states an empirical observation that motivated the work, and separately whether that observation is presented as something the authors established rather than assumed or cited; score 0-10 for BOTH together.
criteria.rationale: R4-DH07 ('we show that the unfavorable effect from false negatives is more significant for the large-scale datasets with more semantic concepts' — established, then acted on), R4-DH17 ('we observed that these classifiers were diverse and many of their decisions were complementary'), R4-DH09 ('on examining mistake-severity distributions ... we find'), R4-DL54 ('Our findings are quite intriguing' — an observation-first paper on the other side). Round-2 A19 scored derivation coupling (structure established, then method derived); this scores whether the motivating fact was EARNED.

criteria.name: Poses a specific question and states its answer plainly
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract frames a specific answerable question and then gives the answer in plain terms, rather than describing an area of activity and a contribution to it. Score the question-and-answer structure, not the importance of the question.
criteria.rationale: R4-DH03 ('What is the most effective way to train a small model? ... Is there a middle way ...? We find the answer to be yes'), R4-DH17 ('we asked the question, besides forming an aggregation, whether these representations can be utilized directly'), R4-DH11 ('a crucial problem: where does the knowledge come from?'). Note the overlap risk with the round-2 nuisance 'rhetorical questions' (.5077, routed incidental): that one counts question marks, this one requires an answer to be given. The pair is a live test of whether the judge can hold the distinction.

criteria.name: Checks whether a trivial approach would have sufficed
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract reports comparing against a deliberately trivial, naive, or degenerate alternative — random selection, the unmodified baseline, a no-op — in order to establish that the proposed machinery is needed at all. Score NA when no comparison of any kind is reported.
criteria.rationale: R4-DH23 constructs trivial recalibration approaches precisely to show they can look state-of-the-art; R4-DH16 tests naive pre-training strategies and reports negative transfer; R4-DL53 notes 'Only the proposed algorithm outperforms random sampling on CIFAR100'. The bank has nothing scoring whether the null option was checked.

criteria.name: Evaluation conditions match the conditions the claim is about
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge what conditions the abstract's claim is about (a deployment setting, a scale, a data regime), and separately whether the reported evaluation was run under those conditions; score 0-10 for the MATCH. Score low when a claim about practice is supported only by small or idealised experiments.
criteria.rationale: R4-DH13 (claims inductive generalisation to any KG, evaluates on 57 different KGs), R4-DH16 (claims downstream transfer, evaluates across multiple downstream molecular and protein tasks), R4-DL51 (claims scalability, evaluates on a >1TB benchmark) versus R4-DH12, which claims a general optimizer and validates on a 95k-parameter 'semi-realistic' network. Round-1 A04 counted evaluation breadth; this scores whether the evidence is of the right KIND for the claim.

criteria.name: Reports variability across seeds, splits, or runs
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract indicates that results were checked for stability across random seeds, data splits, or repeated runs — including reporting that instability was found. Score NA when the abstract reports no empirical results.
criteria.rationale: R4-DL35 ('our empirical findings highlight the strong sensitivity of several recent GNNs to the random seed used for data splitting'), R4-DL41 ('propose a new metric (pass^k) to evaluate the reliability of agent behavior over multiple trials', reporting 'terribly inconsistent'). Bank item 147 ('Randomness control and experimental repeats reporting') exists but is phrased for biomedical repeats and returns NA on almost every ML abstract, so this is the ML-native version.

criteria.name: Corrects a specific prior claim rather than adding to a pile
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the contribution is positioned as correcting, qualifying, or overturning an identifiable prior claim or widely-held position, as opposed to adding one more method to an existing family. Score low for 'we propose X, which outperforms Y'.
criteria.rationale: R4-DH09 (corrects the claim that hierarchy-aware classifiers make better mistakes), R4-DH15 (corrects reliance on the faithfulness assumption), R4-DL35 ('we both challenge and leverage this assumption' about homophily), R4-DL54 (corrects the expectation that contrastive methods degrade under imbalance). Related to round-3 A36 (overturns a stated prior belief) but scoped to a specific CLAIM in the literature rather than a diffuse field belief; both may fire together and the correlation is worth measuring.

criteria.name: Cost accounting includes the method's own overhead
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract reports a saving or speedup, and separately whether the accounting visibly includes what the method itself costs (its training, its extra passes, its added parameters); score 0-10 for BOTH together. Score low for a headline speedup whose own overhead is not accounted for.
criteria.rationale: R4-DH00 ('requiring 20-33% fewer FLOPs compared to standard training' — the comparison is total-cost), R4-DH02 (80.7% top-1 at 194M FLOPs, then 80.0% at 100M FLOPs), R4-DH03 ('at a slightly higher cost than supervised learning from scratch' — the overhead is stated). Paired with a shallow Track-B probe counting multiplicative-speedup notation, to test whether the judge separates accounting from advertising.

criteria.name: Leaves a transferable design principle, not only a method
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract states a lesson or principle a reader could apply outside this paper's specific method, and separately whether that principle is grounded in the reported results rather than merely suggested; score 0-10 for BOTH together.
criteria.rationale: R4-DH16 ('the key to the success of our strategy is to pre-train at the level of individual nodes as well as entire graphs' — a stated principle, backed by the negative-transfer result), R4-DH27 (tilting as a general lever), R4-DL54 ('a representation model generating a balanced feature space can generalize better'). Distinct from round-2 A20 (reusable ARTIFACT) and round-3's portability criterion: this is a reusable IDEA, and it should correlate negatively with artifact-delivery papers.

criteria.name: Includes a condition under which the method is expected to do badly
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the reported evaluation includes a setting chosen to stress or break the proposed approach — an adversarial case, an out-of-distribution regime, a condition the authors expect to be hard — as opposed to only favourable settings. Score NA when no evaluation is reported.
criteria.rationale: R4-DH12 ('we experimentally verify our algorithm's performance in the presence of noise'), R4-DL55 (a benchmark built specifically to defeat contamination, reporting that models' true abilities are lower), R4-DL41 (reports state-of-the-art agents succeeding on <50% of tasks). Round-3 A40 scored stating what the method does NOT do; this scores actually TESTING where it breaks.

criteria.name: Credits what prior work got right while stating what it missed
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract acknowledges a genuine contribution of the work it builds on or displaces, and separately whether it states specifically what that work leaves unsolved; score 0-10 for BOTH together. Score low for prior work described only as limited, and low for prior work praised with no gap identified.
criteria.rationale: R4-DL44 ('UniFormer has successfully alleviated this issue ... However, this model has to require a tiresome and complicated image-pretraining phrase'), R4-DH00 ('While this is appealing since it yields resource and wall-time savings, it has limitations, particularly ...'), R4-DH04 (credits regret minimisation's role before extending it). Bank item 70 scores citation coverage and item 103 citation ethics; neither scores the balance of credit and critique.

criteria.name: Reports the number a skeptic would ask for
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract volunteers the specific quantity most likely to undercut its own claim — the accuracy given up for a speedup, the failure rate, the gap remaining to a stronger method, the cost of the fix — rather than only the quantity that flatters it.
criteria.rationale: R4-DL42 volunteers '2.19% accuracy loss' alongside its 91x energy claim; R4-DH00 gives both FLOP savings and downstream gains; R4-DH03 concedes 'a slightly higher cost'. Contrast R4-DL33 and R4-DL52, which report gains without the corresponding concession. Related to round-2 A23 (cost together with gain) but scores VOLUNTEERING the unflattering number specifically, which is an honesty signal rather than a completeness one.
